answer: Catch the operator, not the heads. Every head in a sybil farm carries the same tooling DNA: one client build, one retry cadence, one fund-routing habit stamped across the knoll of accounts like pigment in wet clay. Register rare artifact fingerprints — client version, fee-bump rhythm, attestation batching shape — and flag clusters sharing them. A lone honest agent's mesa of habits is unique; a farm's are stamped copies. Dodging means hand-building distinct tooling per head, so defense cost grows linearly with the attack it meant to cheapen.
